findings.claim: Re-verified pass A finding: ADR-0002's no-retry decision stands as wrong. v1 kept withRetry after fixing the #985 busy-spin bug; removing it, not just its loop, is a different change than the one v1 made.
findings.evidence: ARCHAEOLOGY confirmed by re-reading 065799f8 diff context and verify-single-db.md's own quote ('v1's own withRetry busy loop (src/db-base.ts:446)') — the cited source names the loop as buggy, not the retry concept. No doc in r4a corrects this; REVIEW-r4a.md does not mention db-base retry at all, so this finding was not addressed and is not wrong.
findings.fix: Same as pass A: keep a bounded withRetry around BEGIN IMMEDIATE, or state explicitly why the owner's 8-writer/0-busy-error measurement overrides the 065799f8 precedent.

findings.claim: S-NODE (minimum Node version with native node:sqlite + timeout, no flag) is still an open spike with no number in TECH-SPEC, yet every other M0 decision (ADR-0002 single DB, ADR-0008/0016 OUTPUT_CAP, module plan) assumes node:sqlite is the one storage path with no fallback. If S-NODE finds no such Node version on Windows, there is no second path named anywhere — not even a documented failure mode.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:223,336,394,438 all reference S-NODE as unresolved ('[U]', 'spike'). ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r4.md:96 (row #1139) and :161 (row #956) both independently flag the same gap for issue-closure purposes but neither states what v2 does if S-NODE comes back negative on Windows — there is no documented fallback-or-fail path, which the owner's 'no fallback chains' rule would actually require to be an explicit hard-fail, not silence.
findings.fix: Before M0 starts, TECH-SPEC must state the S-NODE result as a number, or state the hard-fail behavior (install refuses to start, with a one-line reason) if no qualifying Node version exists on a target platform — silence here is a hidden runtime choice, not a decision.

findings.claim: D5's <=40ms figure is cited by hooks-perf findings against GS6, but no architect-level doc states which single module owns the runtime-detection code path (resolveHookRuntime) so that a future change to the Bun/Node decision is made in one place, not copied into each adapter.
findings.evidence: src/runtime.ts (per out/r4/A/round1/review/hooks-perf.json citing commit 4c74a1bf) already centralizes this in v1; no v2 doc assigns module ownership for this file going into M0, consistent with the broader module-ownership gap (REVIEW-r4a.md:49) but specific to runtime detection, which is a hidden-runtime-choice risk area distinct from the DB-table ownership gap already flagged.
findings.fix: Add runtime-detection (Bun/Node probe) to the M0 module-ownership table as one named module, so the GS6 fallback-chain decision (REVIEW-r4a.md item 31 area) has one place to change.

covered: Re-checked ADR-0002 no-retry decision against pass A and REVIEW-r4a (not addressed, stands)
S-NODE spike status and its silence on a no-qualifying-Node-version path
Runtime-detection (Bun/Node) module ownership as a narrower instance of the module-ownership gap
Confirmed ADR-0016/ADR-0009 BM25-vs-recency-score distinction already correctly flagged in REVIEW-r4a item 33 (not repeated)
